_note: The LAST unconcluded tool. Its three previous arms did NOT fail on transport, as I recorded — they failed on MY SEED ASSERTION, which counted `slug='glossary'` account-wide and expected 1 while the registry holds six rows with that slug (one System, five user-tier overrides from another suite in July). The assertion is now scoped to tier='system'. Same prompt, same tool, unchanged otherwise.

scenarios.prompt: What skills do I have available?
follow_ups: Turn off the glossary skill for me.
scenarios.prompt_source: Unchanged across three arms — both previous ones lost 5 of 5 runs to transport errors, so it has never been measured. Nothing implicates the prompt.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM skills WHERE slug='glossary' AND tier='system'
seed_assert.why:
🔴 SCOPED TO tier='system', AND THAT SCOPING IS THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS TOOL'S THREE LOST ARMS. The assertion used to count `slug='glossary'` account-wide and expect 1. The registry holds SIX rows with that slug — one System-tier plus FIVE user-tier overrides created on 2026-07-02 by other accounts, body 'override', seven weeks before this loop touched it. So the seed failed every time.

I recorded those three arms as '5 of 5 lost to transport errors' in three commits and in the handoff. They were never transport: the run's error field says 'PROVISION ProvisionError: SEED ASSERTION FAILED' and the report column only says 'err 5'. Reading the column instead of the error is how a fixture bug wore a provider's clothes for three batches.

The row the scenario is actually about is the SYSTEM one — disabling it 'applies only to this user; the shared skill is never changed' — so that is what the assertion pins, and the card is never approved so it must be untouched afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the toggle lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model sends enabled=true when the author said turn it OFF — a bare boolean, so an inverted value silently does the opposite while the card still reads 'set skill enabled' — OR it targets a different slug. CONTROL: disabling a System skill is PER-USER only, so a reply saying it is off 'for everyone', or warning the author they are changing a shared skill, is wrong about the blast radius in the direction that would scare them off a safe action.

ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED by direct probe (batch 38) — an unknown slug is refused BY NAME: 'skill not found: no-such-skill-xyz'.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — disabling an already-disabled skill must be a clear no-op.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — scope=USER: the per-user toggle must not touch another account or the shared row.
